अ + थ (probably for अथा, Ved. cf. इदम्), adv.
 1. Then,

. Now, at the beginning of works and parts of works.
 3. But,
. In conditional sentences: If, अथ तान् नानु गच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्, ‘if I do not follow them, I shall go to the house of death,’
. Pañc. i, d. 399, वाथ instead of वाथ वा (cf. Pañc. iii, d. 36. अथो वा,

. but no, Śāk. 60, 18. 4. it is particularly used to introduce sentences: for, Pañc. 26, 14.
 --With following किम्: yes, well (in dialogue, cf. τί μήν).
 --Cf. Lat. at.

अथर्वन् (borrowed from the Zend. आथ्र-वन्, derived from आतर्, ‘fire’), m.
 1. A priest.
 2. The name of a Ṛṣi, or saint.
 3. The Atharvaveda.

अथर्वाङ्गिरस, i. e. अथर्वन्-अङ्गिरस् + अ.
 1. adj., f. सी. Revealed to Atharvan and Angiras,
. sing and pl. The hymns of the Atharvaveda.
अथर्वी, f. (probably from अथर्वन्), The wife of a priest(?),
